## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Pañcapaṇḍitajātaka* (Ja 508) is a canonical Jātaka tale whose full narrative is traditionally deferred in the commentary to the *Mahā-ummaggajātaka* (*Mahāummagge āvisabhavissati*) [Fausböll 1887; SuttaCentral]. The verses associated with the story address the theme of keeping a secret and the qualities of statecraft: the Bodhisatta advises the king never to disclose his secrets to anyone, contrasting with hostile counselors who argue that confiding in a wife, friend, brother, son, or mother is acceptable [Ānandajoti 2010]. Additional verse instruction emphasizes discerning profit and loss, recognizing what has been done and left undone, punishing those who deserve censure, and supporting those worthy of favor [Ānandajoti 2010].
Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal links across the Pali corpus, identifying matches with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (both the fourth and sixth volumes), the *Paṇḍaranāgarājajātaka* (Ja 518, sharing segments §17.4–22.4), and the didactic collection *Nīti-gantha-saṅgaho Naradakkhadīpanī* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages of the text with the Tibetan *Nītiśāstra* (D4335) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].
